requirement_text.REQ-369: Distinct PlatformDashboardPage for PLATFORM_ADMIN — replaces the shared tenant-branded landing page for that role, with role-conditional login routing. Fixes the gap ISS-0700 found and REVIEWER's determination on it (docs/issues/ISS-0700.yaml, determined_by: REVIEWER, determined_at: 2026-09-17T13:52:00Z, path: missing-functionality) scoped for REQ-ANALYST to fill in. ISS-0700 stays status: open as the source finding — this requirement is the fix, tracked separately; do not close ISS-0700 from this requirement's own close-out. Prior art: lib/letflow/design/req360-platform-login-routing-uat-scenario.md's Section 0 finding #1 and Section 7 OQ-3, which first surfaced this exact open question and explicitly declined to resolve it, and REQ-360's own entry in this file (its description was corrected by ISS-0700's DOC-UPDATER partial_action to state the current, factual shared-'/'-root behaviour — this requirement is what makes that description stale again, in the intended direction). THE PROBLEM, CONFIRMED BY DIRECT READ (not re-derived here, see ISS-0700's diagnosis/determination blocks for the full trace). web/src/router.tsx mounts the identical `<TenantDashboardPage />` at both `{ index: true }` and `{ path: 'dashboard' }` for every authenticated role, PLATFORM_ADMIN included. web/src/pages/dashboard/TenantDashboardPage.tsx is actively tenant-possessive — its `<h1>` renders `tenantDisplayName` from `useTenantContext()`, and its copy reads "Welcome to your BPM workspace." PLATFORM_ADMIN has no natural tenant to bind that to (confirmed via lib/letflow/design/req128-keycloak-dev-stack.md — PLATFORM_ADMIN is a realm role inside the shared realm, not a tenant). Two broken outcomes result depending on how they land: a misleading "your workspace" framing if they land through a tenant-branded realm slug, or the actively broken `isUnknown` banner ("Unknown workspace" / "Tenant name could not be loaded. Contact your administrator.") if they land with no realm slug — the more likely path for a platform admin, per REVIEWER's determination. SCOPE — THREE CHANGES, ALL IN web/. (1) A new `web/src/pages/dashboard/PlatformDashboardPage.tsx`, sibling to `TenantDashboardPage.tsx` in the same directory, rendering platform-wide, non-tenant-branded content only — it must not import or call `useTenantContext()` at all, and must not render `tenantDisplayName` or the "your workspace"/`isUnknown` copy anywhere. Concretely: an `<h1>` (`data-testid="platform-dashboard-heading"`) reading "Platform Overview" (a fixed string, not derived from any tenant); a tenant-count tile (`data-testid="tile-tenant-count"`) sourced from the EXISTING `tenantsApi.list()` (web/src/api/tenants.ts, `/api/v1/tenants`, already used by web/src/pages/admin/tenants/TenantsPage.tsx) reading its response's `total` field — do not invent a new backend endpoint for this; and a "Platform Admin Links" quick-links section (`data-testid="platform-quick-links"`) with router `<Link>`s into the existing `/admin/tenants`, `/admin/services`, `/admin/health`, `/admin/metrics`, `/admin/users` routes (all already built and already gated to PLATFORM_ADMIN in AppShell.tsx's NAV_ITEMS — this requirement only links to them, it does not change or duplicate their content). Follow this codebase's existing self-gating precedent for PLATFORM_ADMIN-only pages (e.g. web/src/pages/admin/tenants/TenantsPage.tsx's `if (!session?.roles.includes('PLATFORM_ADMIN'))` guard, web/src/pages/admin/HealthDashboardPage.tsx's `isPlatformAdmin` check) — PlatformDashboardPage must render an equivalent "not authorized" state for a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN who reaches the route directly by URL, since (per the existing pattern this project already uses everywhere else) routes are not role-gated at the router level, only self-gated per page. (2) `web/src/router.tsx` gains a new sibling route under the existing authenticated route tree (e.g. `{ path: 'platform-dashboard', element: <PlatformDashboardPage /> }`), alongside the existing unchanged `{ index: true }` and `{ path: 'dashboard' }` entries — those two stay exactly as they are today (`TenantDashboardPage`, for every non-PLATFORM_ADMIN role, and reachable by PLATFORM_ADMIN too if they navigate there directly, since this requirement does not remove that page's general reachability). (3) `web/src/pages/OidcCallbackPage.tsx`'s unconditional `navigate('/', { replace: true })` (line 72) becomes role-conditional: PLATFORM_ADMIN (checked via the already-decoded `payload.roles`, which this file already reads at line 39 but does not yet use for routing) navigates to `/platform-dashboard` instead; every other role's navigation target is unchanged (`/`). OUT OF SCOPE, EXPLICITLY — DO NOT FOLD IN. The separate "Unknown workspace" banner gap REVIEWER flagged but did not fold into this requirement's frame: unauthenticated/no-realm-slug users of ANY non-PLATFORM_ADMIN role still hitting TenantDashboardPage's `isUnknown` banner path is a related-but-separate pre-existing concern, not resolved by this requirement and not this requirement's job to fix — leave TenantDashboardPage's own isUnknown handling untouched. Cross-tenant health/metrics AGGREGATION beyond what HealthDashboardPage/MetricsPage already compute is also out of scope — this requirement links to those existing pages, it does not build new cross-tenant aggregation logic or a new summary endpoint. Depends on REQ-360, whose permanent UAT scenario (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/platform-login-routing-by-role.yaml) currently documents the real (pre-fix) shared-'/'-root behaviour this requirement changes for PLATFORM_ADMIN specifically — that scenario's PLATFORM_ADMIN branch needs updating to assert the new `/platform-dashboard` destination as part of this requirement's own close-out (same file, same branching construct, no new UAT infrastructure needed), matching REQ-360's AC3 discipline (document the real, current behaviour, don't let a scenario go stale against it).

acceptance_criteria: web/src/pages/dashboard/PlatformDashboardPage.tsx exists, renders `data-testid="platform-dashboard-heading"` with the fixed text "Platform Overview" (never a tenant name), never calls `useTenantContext()`, and never renders `tenantDisplayName` or the `isUnknown` "Tenant name could not be loaded" copy anywhere in its output — verified by a component test asserting both the presence of the fixed heading and the absence of any tenant-branded string

the tenant-count tile (`data-testid="tile-tenant-count"`) renders a real count sourced from `tenantsApi.list()`'s `total` field (no new backend endpoint introduced), covered by a test that mocks the existing `/api/v1/tenants` response and asserts the rendered count matches the mocked `total`

a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN session reaching `/platform-dashboard` directly by URL sees a self-gated not-authorized state (matching this codebase's existing per-page role-guard precedent, e.g. TenantsPage.tsx/HealthDashboardPage.tsx), covered by a test asserting a PROCESS_OPERATOR (or any non-PLATFORM_ADMIN) session does not see the platform content

web/src/router.tsx has a new route for PlatformDashboardPage alongside the unchanged existing `{ index: true }` and `{ path: 'dashboard' }` TenantDashboardPage entries — both old entries are provably unchanged (diff shows only an addition, no modification to the existing two lines)

web/src/pages/OidcCallbackPage.tsx navigates a PLATFORM_ADMIN session to `/platform-dashboard` and every other role's session to `/` unchanged, covered by two component/integration tests (one per branch) asserting the actual `navigate()` target based on `payload.roles`

a real PLATFORM_ADMIN login against the live QA environment is exercised end-to-end (reusing REQ-358's environment-targeting UAT infrastructure) and actually lands on `/platform-dashboard` with the real tenant count rendered — not merely unit-tested — with the result (including a screenshot, per UAT-RUNNER's existing screenshot-as-primary-evidence discipline) quoted in this requirement's close-out

test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/platform-login-routing-by-role.yaml's PLATFORM_ADMIN branch is updated to assert `/platform-dashboard` as the destination (not the old shared `/` root), re-run for real against QA per REQ-360's own verification discipline, with the updated pass result quoted; the scenario's other branches (tenant-scoped role, unauthenticated) are left unchanged since this requirement does not alter their behaviour

this requirement's own close-out states explicitly that ISS-0700 remains status: open (not closed by this requirement) and that the separate 'Unknown workspace' banner gap for non-PLATFORM_ADMIN unauthenticated/no-realm-slug users is unresolved and out of this requirement's scope
